metadata.case_name: TSANG YUET SHAN v. TSUEN KING HOME FOR THE AGED LTD AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: soft tissue contusion to the lower back and coccyx region
source: the plaintiff only suffered from a soft tissue contusion to the lower back and coccyx region.

Dr. Ko opined that "no significant residues" was expected from the accident based on "objective findings", and that "in usual clinical situation", this "soft tissue contusion" would be adequately treated by conservative treatment "up to about 6 months".
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of lower back or pelvis

manifestations.description: persistent coccyx region pain spreading to the lower back
flare-up episodes of severe pain causing difficulties getting out of bed, putting on trousers or going to the bathroom
interference with sleep (pain would wake her up 1-2 times a week requiring stretching before sleeping)
inability or difficulty to perform housework (could not change sheets on a bed, move a bed mattress, clean the floor, wash the dishes)

treatments_received.treatment: Attendance at A&E of Yan Chai Hospital
source: The plaintiff attended A&E of Yan Chai Hospital after the accident and the records showed that she had sustained buttock injury with tenderness at the coccygeal region but the x-ray revealed no fracture of the coccyx.

a MRI was performed on 9 October 2012 which showed "no significant abnormality except for a small annular tear" which "should not be related to the subject accident" (as agreed by both Orthopaedics experts in the JMR: Trial Bundle page 412 paragraphs 179 and 180).
Another MRI was performed on 9 October 2012 which showed "no significant pathology but pre-existing mild degenerative changes". (Dr. Ko at Trial Bundle page 412 paragraph 177).
the plaintiff had since attended various doctors, pain clinic, physiotherapists and clinical psychologists
the plaintiff had since attended various doctors, pain clinic, physiotherapists and clinical psychologists

During the hearing, the plaintiff claimed that she could cope with regular pain-killers but there were "flare-up" episodes when the pain was so bad that she had difficulties getting out of bed, putting on trousers or going to the bathroom.
the plaintiff had received three caudal block injections.
At one point, the plaintiff said her pain was 30-40% better after her third caudal block injection but later said that the pain was the same.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultations with various doctors and Chinese Medical Practitioners
source: the plaintiff had since attended various doctors, pain clinic, physiotherapists and clinical psychologists
the plaintiff in this case attended multiple doctors, Chinese Medical Practitioners and medical departments and had taken 2 MRIs scans on her own initiative.

treatments_received.treatment: Past medical expenses claimed (claimed HK$20,000; court estimated and awarded HK$1,600)
source: The plaintiff claims HK$20,000 as past medical expenses spanning some 6 1/2 years (or 78 months) but as the court finds that the plaintiff would have recovered within 6 months (according to Dr. Ko) so a reasonable estimation of medical expenses is HK$20,000/78 x 6 = HK$1,538. I would round this up to HK$1,600.
The court would allow HK$2,500 as claim for tonic food but this would be generous given that this was a soft tissue contusion injury.
The court would allow HK$1,000 as traveling expenses.

losses.description: Persistent coccyx and lower back pain with mild reduction of motion and tenderness affecting daily comfort and causing flare-ups
